title: "Whatever you do, offer it" (9.26–9.28)
hook: one verse turns eating, giving and every ordinary chore into worship

segments.voice: Yesterday: the one who offers a leaf, and Sudama's handful of rice. Your line was a leaf, a flower, water. Did you give one small thing with love? Today the offering gets bigger. Much bigger. Day one hundred ninety-one.

Walk into many Hindu kitchens before a meal and watch. Before anyone eats, a small portion is set aside, sometimes on a little plate in front of an image of Krishna or at the family shrine. A moment, maybe a verse. Then the food comes back to the table, and it isn't just lunch anymore. It's prasad, grace, a gift returned. Yesterday's verse was about a leaf. But a leaf is one thing. What about the rest of the day? The dishes, the email, the commute, the argument about whose turn it is to take out the trash? Today, one verse that takes all of it.
screen: `A PORTION SET ASIDE.` → `LUNCH BECOMES PRASAD.` → `WHAT ABOUT THE REST OF THE DAY?`

segments.voice: Verse twenty-seven: whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever discipline you practice, Arjuna, do it as an offering to me. In Sanskrit it's a list with a drumbeat: yat karoshi, whatever you do; yad ashnasi, whatever you eat; yaj juhoshi, whatever you offer into the fire; dadasi yat, whatever you give; yat tapasyasi, whatever effort you make. Five whatevers. And then one instruction: tat kurushva mad-arpanam, make it an offering to me. Look at the list. It starts with the most general thing, doing, and the second item is eating. Not meditating, not reading scripture. Eating. The Gita puts lunch right next to sacrifice. Yesterday Krishna asked for a leaf. Today he asks for the whole day. Not more stuff; more of your ordinary life, turned in a direction. And verse twenty-eight says what happens. You'll be freed from the bonds of action, with its good and bad fruits. With your mind set on this yoga of letting go, you'll be free, and you'll come to me. This is where chapter three's work without attachment and chapter four's sacrifice come together. The easiest way to stop clutching the fruit of an action is to give it away before you start. That's the word today: whatever you do. The shortest summary of the Gita some people know. Offer everything.
screen: `FIVE WHATEVERS.` · `EATING, RIGHT NEXT TO SACRIFICE.` · `NOT MORE STUFF. MORE OF YOUR DAY.` · `FREED FROM THE BONDS OF ACTION.` · then, large: `OFFER EVERYTHING.`

segments.voice: Sit, and walk through the five whatevers for today. What will you do? Picture one task. What will you eat? Picture one meal. What will you give? One small thing. What effort will you make? One hard moment. For each one, take a breath and imagine handing it over before it happens: this is offered. If you pray, you can offer it to Krishna, as the verse says. The bell holds the time.
Whatever you do. Gita nine, twenty-seven: whatever you do, eat, offer, give or strive for, make it an offering.
Your line: offer everything. Pick one ordinary chore today, the dishes, the laundry, the drive, and do it as an offering from start to finish. Day one hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Many Hindus offer food to God before eating (naivedya) and receive it back as prasad, and many try to dedicate their daily work as an offering in the spirit of Gita 9.27.

match.prompt: the five whatevers — tap the pairs.

myth: verse 27 only talks about temple rituals
it lists doing, eating, offering, giving and effort; eating is second on the list.
verse 28 says offering action frees you from its bonds
freed from the bonds of action with its good and bad fruits.
prasad is food that has first been offered to God
set aside as an offering, then received back as a gift of grace.

fork.setup: Krishna lists five things to do as an offering to him. which is second on his list?
fork.reveal: whatever you eat, right after whatever you do. the Gita puts lunch next to sacrifice.

original.note: Sanskrit: mad-arpanam, as an offering to me; mat (me) + arpana (offering, handing over).

trapdoor: what you thought: worship happens at the temple.
what it means: whatever you do, eat, give or strive for can be offered; the whole day becomes worship.

what a scholar hears: 9.27's list, yat karoshi yad ashnasi yaj juhoshi dadasi yat, yat tapasyasi, runs from ordinary acts to ritual and ascetic ones; 9.28 ties it to sannyasa-yoga, gathering up chapters 3 to 5.
